implementation_notes: Same runtime split as JavaScript—net.Server/http.Server own acceptance and hand each connection to a handler—while TypeScript adds static types (Server, Socket and ConnectionListener). Use net.createServer((socket: net.Socket) => ...) without a generic type parameter; http.createServer() produces IncomingMessage + net.Socket pairs. For TLS, tls.createServer() yields TLSSocket instances. Framework layers (Fastify, Nest and Express) still sit on the same runtime acceptor.
pitfalls: Types hide runtime pitfalls: 'error' and 'close' handling is not optional — always add socket.on('error', ...) and server.on('error', ...).
A slow handler buffers writes; use stream back-pressure (pause/resume) instead of assuming flow control.
Do not re-implement acceptance above http.Server internals; intercepting 'connection' breaks keep-alive expectations.
socket.setKeepAlive(true, initialDelay) may be called while the socket is open; it configures TCP keep-alive but does not replace application-level liveness or framing.
Server.listen() callback fires once; use server.on('listening', ...) for reliable post-bind setup.
